prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1250; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers were dispatched to a low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas. Driver 1 and Driver 2 were operating their vehicles when the front ends made contact. Driver 1 was seated in the vehicle when officers arrived and was seen there by the responding officer, and Passenger, who was in the front seat, confirmed that Driver 1 had been driving. Driver 1 reported neck strain and said the force of the impact pushed them forward and back against the seat. Based on the direction and force of the collision, that account is consistent with the damage to both vehicles, which is largely in line with the reported impact. Scene photographs show several of the damaged areas described by the drivers. No independent witnesses were located. Driver 2 reported no prior damage to their vehicle, and nothing at the scene suggested earlier damage to Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the insurance policy for the vehicle involved.
